title: Cisco CUBE, CUCM, and Unity Connection
summary: CUBE as an IOS XE B2BUA, the dial-peer and SIP profile tools, and the CUCM and Unity documents that use different objects with similar names.

lessons.title: CUBE is an IOS XE B2BUA
lessons.summary: Cisco Unified Border Element is a B2BUA on IOS XE. It shares the IOS voice stack with other voice features.
objectives: Name CUBE as Cisco Unified Border Element
Place it in the B2BUA role
Treat IOS voice behavior as release-specific

illustration.title: CUBE on IOS XE
illustration.caption: Basic SIP configuration and SIP profiles are separate chapters of the same product.

layers.name: CUBE
layers.detail: Cisco Unified Border Element, a B2BUA

layers.name: Dial peers
layers.detail: Where the next hop is selected

paragraphs: CUBE means Cisco Unified Border Element. On IOS XE it is a B2BUA: a UAS toward the caller and a UAC toward the next hop.
The basic SIP configuration guide and the SIP profiles guide are the two chapters this track cites for that behavior. RFC 7092 is the taxonomy for the role itself.

sections.h: Same voice stack, confirm the release
paragraphs: CUBE shares the IOS voice stack with other IOS voice features. A control documented for CME or SRST can exist on the same stack, and the reader must confirm behavior on their release.
Do not treat a blog’s version gate as newer than the guides. Inbound SIP profile support is discussed in the use-case technote. The 17.6 and later profile syntax lives in the SIP profiles guide.

sections.h: Trusted sources on the shared stack
paragraphs: Under voice service voip, ip address trusted list names sources the IOS voice stack is willing to accept. The CME toll-fraud chapter and the SRST guide both document that list.

CUBE shares this stack, so confirm the behavior on your release. The CME and SRST guides do not publish one shared maximum list size, and this course states no maximum. The list is a defensive control for peers you intend to accept, such as 198.51.100.30 and 192.0.2.40.

lessons.title: Dial peers select the SIP next hop
lessons.summary: dial-peer voice N voip, session protocol sipv2, and session target ipv4: name a SIP next hop.
objectives: Read the three documented dial-peer lines
Point session target at the intended peer
Keep extra IOS commands out of this lesson

illustration.title: Lines this lesson is allowed to teach
illustration.caption: Matching keys beyond these lines are in the configuration guide for your release.
columns: What it does in this lab
rows: Sends that peer to the carrier

paragraphs: A CUBE next hop is a dial peer. The form taught here is dial-peer voice N voip, then session protocol sipv2, then session target ipv4: followed by the peer address.
In the synthetic, dial peer 200 targets 192.0.2.40, the carrier. Dial peer 100 in a design toward CUCM would target 198.51.100.30. N is the tag you choose.

sections.h: What this lesson leaves in the guide
paragraphs: Inbound matching and outbound destination patterns are real IOS behavior. The basic configuration guide for your release is where those commands are printed.
This lesson does not add command lines beyond the three above. If a call hits the wrong peer, capture the outbound INVITE and compare the Request-URI host with session target ipv4:.

lessons.title: voice class sip-profiles
lessons.summary: A voice class sip-profiles rule can add, modify, or remove a header on a named method. Inbound support arrived after Cisco IOS 15.4.
objectives: Read request INVITE sip-header rules
Separate this object from a CUCM SIP profile
Test a rule before blaming the carrier

illustration.title: Profile actions in the documented syntax
illustration.caption: The lab removes Diversion. modify and add are the other two actions.

paragraphs: voice class sip-profiles 10 holds the rule request INVITE sip-header Diversion remove. The same grammar accepts modify or add in place of remove, with the header name in that position.
Applied to an INVITE, remove deletes the named header. The Collaboration Solutions Analyzer SIP Profile Tester is the documented place to try a rule against a message before you load it on a router.

sections.h: Inbound support and the version gate

This lesson does not invent a newer version gate. Confirm on your release whether the profile is applied inbound or outbound, and do not confuse this IOS object with the SIP Profile object on CUCM.

lessons.title: Early offer and delayed offer
lessons.summary: Delayed offer means the INVITE has no SDP. voice-class sip early-offer forced makes the outbound dial peer send an offer in the INVITE.
objectives: Define delayed offer
State where RFC 3264 allows an offer
Name the CUBE command that forces early offer

illustration.title: Two legs, two timings
illustration.caption: RFC 3264 allows the offer in the INVITE or in a reliable response.

paragraphs: Delayed offer means the INVITE has no SDP. The offer comes later. RFC 3264 allows the offer in the INVITE or in a reliable response.

If the offer arrives in a reliable 18x, PRACK carries the answer and 100rel applies. If the offer arrives in the 200 OK, the ACK carries the answer. The caller leg in this synthetic follows that second pattern.
voice-class sip early-offer forced is the documented way to force early offer on a dial peer. The outbound INVITE then contains SDP even though the inbound INVITE from 198.51.100.30 did not.
The two legs can therefore use different offer/answer timings. Capture both. Do not assume the SDP bytes match until you read them.

illustration.title: Same words, different objects
illustration.caption: Do not configure one product with the other product’s syntax.
rows: A CUCM script on a trunk
A CUCM trunk setting in that version’s admin guide

paragraphs: CUCM places calls to CUBE, to a carrier, or to another cluster on a SIP trunk. The lab trunk source is 198.51.100.30 and the CUBE address is 203.0.113.20.

A SIP profile on CUCM is the CUCM object. It is different from CUBE voice class sip-profiles. Lua normalization scripts exist on CUCM for message changes. This lesson does not invent a menu click-path or a script API.
MTP required is a CUCM trunk setting documented in the admin guide for that version — confirm the guide before you check the box. Open the admin guide for the version you run before you enable it.

An MTP inserts a media resource and can change when SDP appears. The synthetic failure in this lesson shows CUCM offering c=198.51.100.30 after the phone offered from 203.0.113.10, which is a reason to read that guide rather than a reason to guess.

sections.h: How the mailbox is indicated in SIP
paragraphs: A forwarded INVITE can carry Diversion with the original called number. Here that value is sip:+15551212@example.com and the reason is unconditional.
History-Info is the other standards-based redirecting header. Whether this version of Unity Connection wants Diversion, History-Info, or both is answered by the SIP integration guide, not by a guess.
